complexity_intro: The complete procedure is summarized in Algorithm \ref{alg:fast_TL-QLDMR}. {\color{blue}Let $T$ denote epochs, $B$ the batch size, and $C_Z$ the cost of selecting the input pool and landmarks. If K-means is used on a pool of size $q$, a dense Lloyd implementation with $r$ initializations and at most $I_K$ iterations per initialization costs $O(rI_Kqmd)$, in addition to pool selection; the clustering cost is absent when the pool itself supplies the landmarks. Dense feature transformation and regularizer construction cost $O(Nm^2)$, kernel evaluation costs $O(Nmd)$, and landmark factorization costs $O(m^3)$. The optimization cost is $O(T[Nm+\lceil N/B\rceil m^2])$. For the exact-kernel comparison, $I_{\mathrm{QP}}$ denotes the number of dense interior-point iterations: each iteration has a cubic dense linear-algebra cost, but the total solve time also depends on the iteration count and requested accuracy.} Table \ref{tab:complexity} summarizes these costs.
intro_framework: To address these challenges, Transfer Learning Quantile Large-margin Distribution Machine for Regression (TL-QLDMR) is proposed as a principled extension of the classical LDMR paradigm for cross-domain probabilistic wind power prediction. {\color{blue}The formulation combines centered source-residual spread control with quantile-dependent pinball loss, constrains the source--target difference along the prediction direction, and weights available target labels separately from source labels. Its contribution is this specified supervised-transfer formulation and its kernel and explicit-feature derivations. The variance term itself is symmetric; the construction is not claimed to be a uniquely optimal quantile-specific variance penalty.
